title: Djenne's traditional houses stand on small hills above floods
body: Djenne in Mali grew into a market on the trans-Saharan trade route. Nearly 2,000 traditional houses survived at the time of UNESCO's account, built on local mounds to keep them above seasonal floodwater.
takeaway: The shape of the ground can be part of a city's flood protection, house by house.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Old Towns of Djenne (1988)
visual: earthen houses clustered on raised ground above a flooded plain

title: Angkor preserves several Khmer capitals in one landscape
body: Angkor Archaeological Park in Cambodia stretches across about 400 square kilometres. It includes remains of different Khmer capitals from the ninth to the 15th centuries, including Angkor Thom with its Bayon temple.
takeaway: The famous temple is one part of a landscape where centres of power changed over centuries.
visual: the stone face towers of the Bayon rising from forest

title: Borobudur has 72 openwork stupas around its upper levels
body: Borobudur was built in central Java in the eighth and ninth centuries. Its upper terraces are circular and carry 72 perforated stone stupas, each containing a statue of the Buddha.
takeaway: The shift from square terraces below to circles above shapes the experience of walking up the monument.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Borobudur Temple Compounds (1991)
visual: perforated bell-shaped stone stupas across a circular terrace at dawn
